subject: Executive weekly roll-up · week of 24 Aug
lead: Four trends with direction, velocity and confidence — not events. Assembled Friday. One is an explicit stability statement.

trends.title: The AI-artifact security category is forming, and JFrog is positioned as the incumbent to displace
trends.body: A third competitor move into model/ML-artifact scanning this quarter (sample). The pattern across releases, hiring and messaging is category formation, not isolated features. Strategic implication: defend the "we were here first" narrative while the category is still being named.

trends.title: Regulation is moving demand toward us: SBOM and vulnerability reporting are becoming procurement preconditions
trends.body: EU CRA reporting duties took effect this week; SBOM mandates are spreading into scope sectors (sample). This is a tailwind — buyers increasingly must have what the platform already produces. Implication: lead regulated-sector GTM with compliance-by-default framing.

trends.title: Competitors are shifting the buying conversation from repository to procurement path
trends.body: A competitor cloud-marketplace listing with committed-spend eligibility appeared this week (sample), following a pattern of moving competition onto deal-mechanics rather than capability. Implication: ensure marketplace and procurement parity is not a silent disadvantage in enterprise cycles.

stability.title: No material change in competitor positioning this week.
stability.detail: Comparison pages, homepages and pricing for all five tracked competitors were captured and diffed. Nothing crossed the materiality threshold. Reporting stability is intelligence, not an empty slot.
